title: Take a tea bag out of a mug of tea: hold it up by its string, squeeze it on the mug's wall with the spoon, plate both
instruction: Take the tea bag out of the mug: squeeze it against the inside of the mug with the teaspoon first, then put the bag and the spoon on the plate.
context: Making a mug of tea with a tea bag is something most people do or watch every day, at home and at work. When the tea has brewed the bag is squeezed against the side of the mug with the teaspoon, so that it does not drip across the worktop on its way out. It takes both hands at once: one holds the bag's string so the bag stays up against the mug's wall just below the rim, the other presses it there with the spoon's bowl, firmly enough to squeeze it out but not so hard that the mug slides or tips. Then the bag is carried out on its string and laid on the plate, and the spoon is laid beside it.
setup: Bench top is z = 0.7475 m (x away from the arms, y to the left); everything is real size and stands on a sheet of white paper, 460 x 460 mm, centred x 0.29, y 0.02, on which drops of tea show. (1) A blue glazed stoneware mug, 94 mm across and 78 mm tall outside (86 mm bore, 72 mm deep), its handle to the left standing 36 mm out, 400 g, holding 220 ml of brewed tea 38 mm deep (620 g in all), centred x 0.22, y 0.00, free to slide or tip. (2) A wet tea bag (filter-paper pillow 52 x 46 x 9 mm, 14 g) standing in the tea against the mug's left inside wall. From its top a 105 mm cotton string runs up over the rim, once round the handle, to a yellow paper tag 26 x 30 mm (2 g) that hangs beside the handle, 100 mm to the left of the mug's axis, its top edge 73 mm above the bench. (3) A stainless teaspoon, 130 mm long (bowl 30 x 42 mm, handle 10 x 4 mm), 28 g, standing in the mug with its bowl on the bottom, leaning on the rim to the right at about 35 degrees from upright, its handle 47 mm proud of the rim. (4) A white side plate with a blue rim, 190 mm across and 6 mm high, centred x 0.395, y 0.00, beyond the mug. Both hands start open above the bench, either side. Real trial: any heavy mug and teaspoon about these sizes, an ordinary string-and-tag tea bag steeped in the mug in room-temperature water (see reset notes), a side plate and a sheet of white paper with the mug's outline drawn on it.
scoring: 0.25: the tea bag lies at rest on the plate. 0.5: also it was squeezed out first: pressed between the teaspoon's bowl and the inside of the mug, over the mug, for 1 s in all, and no gripper finger ever touched the bag. 0.75: also no drop of tea fell on the paper, and the mug stayed put (moved less than 10 mm, never tilted more than 10 degrees). 1.0: also the spoon lies at rest on the plate (its bowl over the plate) and both hands are 8 cm or more from the bag, its tag and the spoon, held for 1 s. The score is 0, whatever else, if the mug slid more than 30 mm or tilted more than 30 degrees at any time (tea spilled). Otherwise 0. Real trial: the video shows the squeeze and that the fingers stay off the bag; drops are counted on the white paper; the mug's shift is measured from its drawn outline with a rule.
reset_notes: One ordinary string-and-tag tea bag per trial: steep it for 1 minute in the mug in room-temperature water coloured with a second bag, then stand the spoon in, take the string once round the handle and let the tag hang. Wipe the spoon and plate; change the paper if a drop fell on it. The grippers hold only the dry tag and the spoon's handle.
fidelity: Isaac Sim 6.1 PhysX, rigid bodies, 240 Hz, no liquid. The wet bag is a rigid pillow: it counts as squeezed out once the spoon has pressed it on the mug's wall with 1.5 N or more (the wall pressing back with 1 N or more; real contact forces) for 1 s. Out of the tea and not squeezed out, it lets a drop fall every 0.5 s (a rule; drops are drawn). The string is a 105 mm length limit, drawn as beads, touching nothing; the tag starts on a hinge that lets go at 1 N. The tea is weight only.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 after 225 of 1,800 steps (11 s); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired (a first attempt ended the same way at step 177). Scripted demo: 1.0 at step 610 (30.5 s). Control, the same demo without the squeeze: 0.25 (4 drops on the paper).
